title: Why Artists Stay Stuck — And How to Get Free
summary: A performed monologue argues that artist identity can narrow a life, then tests a comfort-zone answer through filming, self-implication and volatile paper dialogue. Every diagnosis-like, health, substance, self-harm, success and spiritual claim remains attributed rather than converted into fact or advice.

connections.relationship: The speaker interrupts a general claim about artists and switches to I-statements.
Artist identity is compared to LGBTQA and the sensitive-artist abbreviation; the analogy remains attributed.
A lifelong artist identity is traced to early praise without becoming developmental fact.
Pain, posture, skin and cramped hands are presented as artist badges and self-report.
Honing craft is linked to lost social practice and missed life events.
Broad substance rhetoric narrows into repeated I hurt myself wording.
Better work, sales, shows and audience approval are staged as the inadequate answer.
Generic Disney language bridges audience metrics to the True You narrative.
The disliked YouTube format becomes the speaker's concrete comfort-zone exercise.
Unknown viewers connect online risk to hoped-for public conversation and grounding.
The less-words refrain is tested against repeated urges to cancel filming.
The monologue ends by converting inward conflict into a hug-and-hate exchange with the paper.

source_notes: All 70 source caption records remain aligned exactly once.
Exactly five raw-to-clean changes are accepted: S.A., honing twice, dependably undependable and likely maté.
Meat section remains literal because a grocery-section reading is plausible.
Growing-your-hair, source-of, eating/body and sick-day fragments remain damaged rather than fluently reconstructed.
Artist-stunting, telepathy and childhood-validation claims are attributed rhetoric/theory.
Body, pain, nutrition, caffeine, alcohol, drugs and illness remain self-report or generalization, not medical fact.
I hurt myself is preserved without inferring method, intent, crisis or present status.
Success and audience claims are performed as a wrong solution rather than editorial advice.
The apparent objections, Dave exchange and paper dialogue are performed within one monologue.
Recording-time age, clothing, illness and preferences are not promoted to current biography.
No named speaker turn or voice-enrollment window is published.
No idea is deleted for discomfort, profanity, stigma or contradiction.
